articles.title: Defining the Optimal Timing for Cochlear Implant Activation: A Review of the Literature and Current Practice Variability
articles.abstract: Hearing loss is among the top three non-fatal disabling conditions in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where cochlear implantation (CI), the gold standard for severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss, remains underused. Conventionally, device activation occurs 2–4 weeks postoperatively; however, early activation (EA) within days of surgery has shown promising benefits. Literature reveals inconsistencies in defining EA and late activation (LA). Some studies report device activation as early as 1 to 7 days postoperatively, while others classify activation within 8 to 14 days as either EA or LA. Traditionally, activation has been reported between 9 and 46 days postoperatively. This lack of consensus complicates the development of standardized postoperative activation timelines and impedes evidence-based clinical guidelines. This narrative review aims to compare the outcomes, feasibility, and safety of EA versus traditional activation in CI patients while highlighting the variability in definitions and activation timelines across studies. A thorough literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Google. Seventeen studies were included, comprising 3 systematic reviews, 2 literature reviews, and 12 primary studies. Most studies reported EA on the first postoperative day, demonstrating benefits such as faster auditory rehabilitation, improved speech recognition, reduced anxiety, and higher patient satisfaction. EA was not associated with increased complications and was cost-effective, particularly for patients from remote areas. However, long-term impedance outcomes were similar between EA and LA. In conclusion, first-day EA appears feasible, safe, and beneficial. Still, large-scale prospective studies are needed to establish optimal activation timing and support standardized CI care protocols.

articles.title: Spatial Governance and Regional Coordination in Chinese-Style Modernization: A Policy and Institutional Analysis of the Fifteenth Five-Year Plan
articles.abstract: “十五五”时期是中国基本实现社会主义现代化的关键阶段。本文以《纲要》《建议》及区域战略文本为分析对象，构建“国家整体性—区域协同—空间正义”分析框架，考察区域协调发展的制度逻辑。研究表明，区域协同并非单纯经济政策，而是系统性空间治理制度安排，通过国家战略统筹、跨区合作与功能空间重构推动制度协同。长三角、成渝与长江经济带案例表明，区域协同正从临时协调转向规则化治理。本文贡献在于将区域协同从政策描述提升为制度分析，阐明国家如何通过政策工具实现发展效率、区域公平与整体性的动态平衡。

articles.title: Museum Tourism Experiences and Visitors’ Recommendation Intentions: A Stimulus–Organism–Response Approach
articles.journal: Journal of Law, Psychology, and Communication Studies
articles.abstract: Using the PLA Naval Museum as an empirical setting, this study examines how museum tourism experiences influence visitors’ recommendation intentions through a Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire and analyzed with reliability/validity tests, correlation analysis, and regression modeling. The results indicate that experience-related stimuli—exhibits and display design, educational and cultural value, and environment and service quality—significantly enhance visitors’ affective and cognitive experiences and perceived value, which in turn strengthen their intention to recommend (including willingness to revisit and share experiences). This study provides contextual evidence for applying S-O-R theory to military-themed museum tourism and offers practical suggestions for improving experience design and communication effectiveness in similar museums.

articles.title: Research Advances and Innovative Optimization Routes of Midwifery Models for Advanced-Age Pregnant Women
articles.abstract: Advanced-age parturients (maternal age≥35years at delivery) have become a key population for maternal and infant safety protection due to age-related physiological decline and high incidence of pregnancy complications (e.g., pregnancy-induced hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus). With the global trend of delayed childbearing and the implementation of China’s three-child policy, the number of advanced-age parturients has continued to rise. The traditional physician-led single midwifery model can no longer meet their individualized care needs. This article systematically reviews the research status of midwifery models for advanced-age parturients at home and abroad from 2019 to 2025, analyzing the application scenarios, implementation effects, and existing limitations of various models from two dimensions: "typical international models" (obstetrician-led care, midwife-led continuous care, group prenatal care, etc.) and "domestic innovative practices" (group-based prenatal care, midwife clinics, integrated delivery rooms, MDT multidisciplinary collaboration, etc.). It focuses on comparing the differential advantages of different models in reducing the cesarean section rate, decreasing postpartum complications, and improving the psychological status of advanced-age parturients, and identifies core issues in domestic models, such as "uneven resource allocation, inconsistent evaluation standards, and shortage of midwives". Based on this, an optimization path of "midwife-centered multidisciplinary collaborative model" is proposed, including improving the primary-level service network, establishing a unified evaluation system, and strengthening midwife competency training. This study aims to provide references for enhancing maternal and infant outcomes of advanced-age parturients and promoting the high-quality development of obstetric care.

articles.title: When Scholarship Becomes a Status Competition: A Reverse Review of Rankings, Journal Tiers, and the Quiet Erosion of the University
articles.abstract: This article offers a critical reverse review of the contemporary order of academic evaluation. Rather than asking whether university rankings and journal classification systems accurately describe academic quality, it asks what happens to universities once these instruments begin to define quality in practice. The central argument is that rankings and journal tiers do not merely measure academic life; they reorganize it. Through the language of performance, visibility, and comparison, they reorder institutional priorities, privilege strategic behavior over educational substance, and transform scholarly judgment into a competition for recognizable status signals. Drawing on scholarship on rankings and reactivity, audit culture, academic capitalism, responsible metrics, and cultural capital, the article develops a five-part argument. First, the expansion of performance governance has displaced older understandings of the university centered on teaching, intellectual formation, and the public cultivation of judgment. Second, rankings operate less as mirrors than as machines: they reshape organizational behavior by rewarding commensurable and publicly legible outputs. Third, journal stratification encourages a substitution in which where research is published begins to matter more than what it says. Fourth, these evaluative systems intensify existing inequalities because actors with more time, networks, language resources, and institutional prestige are better positioned to convert indicators into recognition. Finally, the article argues that evaluation becomes most damaging when proxies cease to be auxiliary tools and become sovereign criteria. Methodologically, the essay proceeds as a metacritical review: it synthesizes existing literature not to stabilize an orthodox consensus, but to reassess the evaluative paradigm itself and to clarify the intellectual costs of allowing proxies to govern academic life. The essay does not reject evaluation as such. It argues instead for a recovery of the university as a public institution whose most important goods, including intellectual seriousness, pedagogical attention, and slow inquiry, cannot be exhausted by ranking positions or journal labels.

articles.title: An Inquiry Beneath the Twin Peaks: Examining University Physics Education in Mainland China from the Perspectives of Feynman’s Intuition and Landau’s Rigor
articles.abstract: The essence of physics lies in a synthesis of childlike curiosity and meticulous rigor, used to comprehend the universe. Consequently, the mission of physics education is not merely the transmission of formulas but the cultivation of an exploratory spirit and critical thinking. This paper presents a critical examination of the current state of university-level physics education in mainland China. A profound disconnect is observed between the intrinsic beauty of the discipline and the prevalent pedagogical methods, which often reduce physics to a tool for examinations. Students are frequently found to be proficient in formulaic application but lacking in a deep understanding of the underlying physical pictures, their motivation driven by academic scores rather than genuine interest. To diagnose these issues and propose reforms, we draw upon the pedagogical philosophies of two titans of physics: Richard P. Feynman, who championed intuitive understanding and the joy of discovery, and Lev D. Landau, who epitomized logical rigor and systematic construction of theory. By using their distinct yet complementary approaches as a lens, we analyze the systemic problems in physics education in mainland China, from utilitarian student motivation and flawed evaluation systems to the inadequacy of teaching materials. Ultimately, we argue for a synthetic approach, integrating Feynman’s emphasis on intuition with Landau’s demand for rigor, to forge a new path that revitalizes physics education and restores its true purpose: to inspire a profound and lasting passion for understanding the natural world.

articles.title: Exploring the Mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine Intervention in Ischemic Stroke: A CiteSpace-Based Bibliometric Study and Visualized Analysis
articles.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the research hotspots and emerging trends in the application of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for the intervention of Ischemic Stroke (IS) utilizing CiteSpace. Method: A comprehensive search was conducted for pertinent publications within the Science Citation Index Expanded (SCI-Expanded) of the Web of Science Core Collection, covering the period from its inception to May 5, 2025 AD. Concurrently, relevant literature was sourced from the Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) database, focusing onPKU Core Journals, CSSCI, and CSCD categories, spanning the years 2000 to 2025. CiteSpace was employed to generate a network map, facilitating the identification of leading authors, institutions, countries, keywords, co-cited authors, journals, references, and prevailing research trends. Result: A comprehensive search yielded 1,929 pertinent articles from the SCI-Expanded database and 2,016 relevant documents from the CNKI database. Gao Ying and Wang Lei emerged as the most prolific authors in the SCI-Expanded database, with their publications appearing in various prominent journals. Long Enze and Wang Yi were identified as the authors with the highest citation counts. Leading institutions in this domain include Beijing University of Chinese Medicine and the China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences, with China being recognized as a dominant contributor to the field. The most frequently cited authors and references predominantly address the epidemiology and characteristics of IS. The top ten keywords, characterized by high frequency and median centrality, include activation, neural regeneration, ischemic stroke, cerebral infarction, Alzheimer's disease, rats, oxidative stress, reperfusion injury, cerebral ischemia, and blood-brain barrier. Notably, the keyword "cell death" exhibited the highest citation burst rate, while "molecular docking" ,"network pharmacology," and "cognitive impairment" have emerged as significant research frontiers. The authors with the most prolific output in the CNKI database include Xie Yanming. Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine is recognized as a leading institution in this field. The top ten keywords, identified by their high frequency and median centrality, are as follows: cerebral infarction, acupuncture, cerebral ischemia, traditional Chinese medicine, rats, acupuncture therapy, electroacupuncture, and review. Conclusion: This study conducted a bibliometric analysis using CiteSpace to identify research hotspots and frontiers in the application of TCM for the intervention of IS. The findings indicate that key areas of focus include cell death, molecular docking, network pharmacology, and cognitive impairment as mechanisms by which TCM may influence IS. Emerging research trends are centered on mechanisms such as cell death, neural pathways, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Future research should aim to explore the interactions among these mechanisms in greater depth and elucidate the relationship between IS and TCM, with particular attention to the brain-gut axis, signal transduction pathways, and pyroptosis.

articles.title: 数字文旅场景中的临场感、沉浸体验与游客满意度关系研究
articles.journal: Journal of Law, Psychology, and Communication Studies
articles.abstract: 数字文旅的时代背景下，“心临其境”的临场感对游客满意度具有重要的影响。基于曲阜三孔景区上线运营的MR虚拟混合现实文旅产品，通过引入临场感理论，探究临场感对游客满意度的作用，并将沉浸体验作为中介变量，研究临场感对游客满意度的影响路径。文章依据227份调查问卷进行实证研究，研究发现：临场感正向影响游客满意度，空间临场感和自我临场感二者对游客满意度均起到正向影响作用；沉浸体验在临场感对游客满意度的影响中起到部分中介作用。通过对曲阜三孔景区MR虚拟混合现实文旅产品带给游客的临场感进行分析，解释了临场感对游客满意度的影响路径，并为旅游目的地设计数字文旅产品提供理论依据与实践指导。 Digital cultural tourism increasingly relies on mixed reality (MR) experiences to enhance engagement at heritage destinations. Drawing on presence theory, this study examines how tourists’ sense of presence influences satisfaction in MR-based cultural tourism and whether immersive experience mediates this relationship. Using the MR program at Qufu’s Three Confucius Sites as the empirical context, we analyzed 227 valid questionnaires with regression and bootstrap mediation tests. The results show that presence positively predicts tourist satisfaction; both spatial presence and self-presence are significant drivers. Moreover, immersive experience partially mediates the effects of spatial presence and self-presence on satisfaction. By providing contextual empirical evidence for presence theory in a cultural-heritage MR setting, this study offers practical implications for designing and operating digital cultural tourism products that improve visitor experience and satisfaction.

articles.title: Freedom in the Sound of Tides
articles.abstract: This poem begins from an embodied experience of standing by the sea and explores freedom as something sensed through the body and heard through sound, rather than treated as an abstract ideal. Through wind, tides, sand, seabirds, and changing light, it connects the repetition of the sea with inner resonance and human longing for openness and release. In this way, the poem seeks to engage broader conversations in music and sound studies on rhythm, environmental listening, echo, and affective space.

articles.title: 限期认缴制下股东出资义务加速到期的理论证成与实践路径
articles.journal: Journal of Law, Psychology, and Communication Studies
articles.abstract: 新《公司法》同时确立了有限责任公司的限期认缴制和股东出资加速到期制度，对于资本制度的发展具有一定的积极意义。其在股东与公司及其债权人的利益权衡之间，都相对更为偏向公司及其债权人。对此，文章对股东出资加速到期制度进行具体分析，如明确两类请求权主体的实现路径，“公司不能清偿到期债务”应以“支付不能”为标准，以及将法条规定理解为适用入库规则以保障债权的公平清偿等问题。同时在实践中应衔接好最长认缴期限制度与加速到期制度，以更加充分的发挥其价值。 The newly revised Company Law establishes both the Time-limited Capital Subscription System and the accelerated maturity mechanism for shareholders’ capital contributions, which has positive significance for the development of the corporate capital system. In balancing the interests among shareholders, the company, and its creditors, the new law tends to favor the company and its creditors.This article conducts a specific analysis of the acceleration mechanism of shareholders’ capital contributions, including clarifying the realization paths of the two types of claimants, arguing that “inability to pay” should be adopted as the standard for determining when a company “cannot pay due debts,” and interpreting the statutory provisions as applying the Assets Entry Rule to ensure the equitable satisfaction of creditors’ claims. At the same time, in practice, proper coordination between the maximum subscription period system and the acceleration mechanism is necessary to give full play to their value.

articles.title: MMCCT: A Multi-Medium Framework for Distributed Climate Intelligence and Bounded Local Climate Regulation
articles.abstract: Climate monitoring still relies primarily on satellite remote sensing and fixed ground-station networks. Although these infrastructures provide indispensable regional coverage and long time series, they often lack the spatial, temporal, and cross-medium resolution needed to detect micro-scale climate anomalies in dense urban districts, industrial interfaces, wetland margins, and other heterogeneous environments. Many such anomalies do not arise from atmospheric forcing alone, but from coupled interactions among atmosphere, water, land surface, and human infrastructure. This article proposes MMCCT as a Methods \& Frameworks contribution to distributed climate intelligence and bounded local climate regulation. MMCCT conceptualizes climate intelligence as a four-medium problem and organizes it through three linked layers: an environmental media system, a distributed sensing network integrating UAVs, nano sensors, and ground IoT nodes, and an intelligence and coordination system for data fusion, anomaly indexing, intervention mapping, and recursive learning. To strengthen methodological clarity, the article formalizes environmental state representation, multi-source fusion, anomaly assessment, and bounded intervention selection through a compact set of analytical expressions. It also develops three research questions, three testable propositions, and a validation strategy based on simulation modelling, UAV field experiments, and multi-source data integration. Rather than claiming deterministic control over climate, MMCCT focuses on locally actionable variables such as shading, ventilation, irrigation, water retention, surface treatment, and emissions management. At its core, MMCCT reframes local climate monitoring as a problem of representational resolution across space, time, and medium, thereby providing a transferable analytical architecture for higher-resolution climate intelligence and bounded local response.

articles.title: Meta-Learned Dynamic Distillation for Automated Hyperparameter Optimization in Machine Learning Systems
articles.abstract: We propose a meta-learned dynamic distillation framework for automated hyperparameter optimization in machine learning systems, which adaptively adjusts knowledge transfer intensity between teacher and student models during training. Traditional distillation methods rely on static intensity schedules or manual tuning, often leading to suboptimal performance when faced with dataset shifts or model uncertainty. The proposed method addresses this limitation by formulating distillation intensity as a learnable hyperparameter, optimized in real-time through a bilevel optimization scheme. Our framework integrates three key components: an Adaptive Distillation Controller (ADC) that meta-learns intensity adjustments based on gradient dynamics and validation loss, a bilevel optimization engine that jointly minimizes student loss and intensity regularization, and a curriculum-aware memory buffer that stabilizes training through historical trajectory analysis. The ADC employs a recurrent neural network to dynamically modulate intensity, while the bilevel optimizer ensures efficient meta-gradient computation without unrolled computational graphs. Furthermore, the memory buffer captures gradient variance patterns to inform intensity adjustments, enabling robust adaptation to evolving training conditions. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms conventional static distillation approaches across multiple benchmarks, achieving superior model performance with reduced manual intervention. The unified treatment of hyperparameter optimization and knowledge distillation not only eliminates the need for handcrafted schedules but also provides a principled way to balance task-specific learning and teacher guidance. This work advances the state of automated machine learning by introducing a scalable, adaptive solution for model tuning.

articles.title: Exploring North Korea–China Relations in the Kim Jong-un Era: A Pluralistic Construction from Geopolitics to a Community of Shared Destiny
articles.abstract: Since Kim Jong Un came to power, North Korea has undergone significant changes in areas such as nuclear weapons development, economic reform, and cultural openness. As a traditional ally and key geopolitical partner of North Korea, China’s perceptions and understanding of its development trajectory have exhibited diverse characteristics. This article examines the latest developments in China–North Korea relations during the Kim Jong Un era by analyzing recent political interactions, economic cooperation, cultural exchanges, and efforts to shape international discourse. The study employs a literature review method, drawing on official documents, academic works, and media reports from both China and North Korea. It argues that during the Kim Jong Un era, the two countries have moved beyond traditional security concerns toward a more rational assessment and cultural resonance regarding North Korea’s path to modernization.

articles.title: 扎根乡土：返乡入乡人员绿色创业协同逻辑
articles.abstract: 返乡入乡人员作为乡村振兴战略实施的关键微观主体，其绿色创业是践行“绿水青山就是金山银山”理念的重要生态行动。然而，在返乡入乡绿色创业群体规模持续扩大的背景下，创业存活率偏低、可持续增长动能不足、持续创业意愿弱化等问题日益凸显。在此背景下，云凤模式通过差异化实践探索出了一条可持续的绿色创业路径。本研究基于协同视角，系统解构云凤模式“四化融合”的核心本质，以生态化夯实绿色创业根基、以组织化实现个体向群体的聚合、以合作化推动分散向协同的整合、以数字化完成传统向数字的转型。通过案例分析法，揭示云凤模式成功的关键机制，提炼返乡入乡人员绿色创业的协同逻辑，为其他返乡入乡创业人员提供实践借鉴。 Returning rural entrepreneurs, as key micro-level actors in the implementation of the rural revitalization strategy, engage in green entrepreneurship as a critical ecological practice to realize the vision that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." However, amid the continuous expansion of the green entrepreneurship cohort among returning rural entrepreneurs, challenges such as low survival rates of entrepreneurial ventures, insufficient momentum for sustainable growth, and weakened willingness for continuous entrepreneurship have become increasingly prominent. Against this backdrop, the Yunfeng Model has explored a distinctive and sustainable path for green entrepreneurship through differentiated practices. This study, from a synergistic perspective, systematically deconstructs the core essence of the "fourfold integration" (ecological, organizational, cooperative, and digital) in the Yunfeng Model—specifically, how ecological development consolidates the foundation of green entrepreneurship, organizational integration transforms individual actors into collective entities, cooperative mechanisms aggregate dispersed resources, and digital transformation upgrades traditional practices. Using case study analysis, this research uncovers the key mechanisms underlying the success of the Yunfeng Model, extracts the synergistic logic of green entrepreneurship among returning rural entrepreneurs, and provides practical references for other returning rural entrepreneurs.

articles.title: National Integration and Institutional Coordination under "One Country, Two Systems": Research on the Institutional Innovation Mechanisms of Hong Kong and Macao’s Integration into China’s Overall National Development
articles.abstract: This article examines Hong Kong and Macao’s integration into China’s overall national development from the perspective of national integration and institutional coordination. It develops the concept of “institutional interfacing” to argue that integration is not policy insertion, administrative absorption, or institutional homogenization, but a process through which institutional differences are organized into governable coordination capacities under the coexistence of the “One Country” principle and “Two Systems” differences. Taking rule alignment in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area as a key case, this article analyzes four types of institutional interfaces: legal services and professional qualifications, financial opening and regulatory coordination, public services and status-based rights, and technology innovation and platform governance. The study argues that institutional interfaces can transform the institutional advantages of Hong Kong and Macao into national governance capacity, while also generating institutional friction when responsibilities are unclear, rules are unstable, risk control is insufficient, or public participation remains limited.

articles.title: The Political Economy of Disease: Marx, Social Medicine, and the Production of Health Inequality
articles.abstract: Karl Marx did not formulate a clinical or pathological theory of medicine. His importance for medical thought lies elsewhere: his critique of capitalism repositioned disease and health as problems of labor, class, social reproduction, and public power. Through close conceptual reading, intellectual-historical reconstruction, and critical synthesis, this article develops its argument through three analytical movements. It first examines Marx's account of the laboring body, the working day, machinery, surplus value, and the reproduction of labor-power. It then situates Friedrich Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England as a bridge between political economy and social medicine before tracing the reformulation of these concerns in the political economy of health and health-inequality research. The article proposes a four-domain distributional framework: capitalist institutions organize hazardous exposure, shape embodied susceptibility, stratify access to treatment, and differentiate recovery and cost-bearing. The framework's contribution lies in integrating processes that are often studied separately within a single account of institutional distribution. Marxian political economy therefore contributes to the social understanding of medicine and health by explaining how risks and protections are allocated, not by substituting for biomedical explanation. This perspective neither reduces every illness to class nor attributes later scholarship directly to Marx. Its continuing value is to connect biological mechanisms with the political and economic structures that distribute exposure, vulnerability, care, and the costs of recovery.

articles.title: A Componential Analysis of “Fuck”
articles.abstract: This study examines how effective Componential Analysis (CA), a classic semantic theory, can be used to analyze the many meanings of the English word “fuck”. Componential analysis breaks words into smaller parts called semantic components. The word “fuck” is a good test for this theory because it has a simple concrete meaning but is used in many different concrete and abstract ways. Using examples from the BFSU CQPweb corpus, the study first lists the main ways “fuck” is used. Then, it tries to break down each use into a set of components. The results show that CA works well for the simple, concrete meanings of “fuck,” such as its use for sex or damage. However, the components become too general and vague for uses where “fuck” is mainly used to express strong feelings. The study also notes some problems with the corpus and methods used, which affected the results. Beyond its theoretical evaluation, this analysis offers practical insights and suggests directions for further study. The findings imply that for language pedagogy, teaching a word like fuck effectively requires explicitly addressing its wide meanings and emotions, helping learners navigate its social impact. Methodologically, the challenges encountered, such as complex corpus queries and inconsistent data tagging, highlight the need for better technical training in corpus linguistics for students and researchers. Future research could build on this work by using larger spoken corpora or social media data to more fully capture informal and expressive uses, or by applying a similar analytical approach to other taboo words to test the generalizability of these findings.

articles.title: [Retracted] Steroid-Eluting Implants for Chronic Rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: A Comparative Review of Propel and Sinuva for Post-Endoscopic sinus surgery management
articles.abstract: RETRACTED ARTICLE The Editorial Office of Health Nexus retracts the following article: Siddiqui MK, Anzar M, Hasan A, Shahid AH, Hashmi SQ. Steroid-Eluting Implants for Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps: A Comparative Review of Propel and Sinuva for Post-Endoscopic Sinus Surgery Management. Health Nexus. 2026;2:40–50. doi:10.63802/hn.V2.2026.154 Following a post-publication editorial review, serious concerns were identified regarding the accuracy, traceability, and reliability of the article’s reference list and the evidentiary support for several statements in the manuscript. The concerns included inaccurate bibliographic metadata, DOI-to-title mismatches, incomplete or insufficient product-information citations, and inconsistencies between the reference list, the text, and the summary tables. Because this article is a narrative review, the cited literature forms the foundation of the article’s conclusions. The extent and pattern of the identified issues affect the transparency, verifiability, and reliability of the scholarly record. After further editorial assessment, the Editorial Office determined that a post-publication correction would not be sufficient to resolve these concerns, as the necessary changes would require substantial reconstruction of the article’s evidence base rather than correction of discrete errors. The authors acknowledged the concerns raised by the Editorial Office and requested an opportunity to correct the article. After careful consideration, the Editorial Office maintained the decision to retract the article. This retraction is issued in accordance with the journal’s publication ethics policy and is intended to correct the scholarly record. It does not, by itself, constitute a finding of research misconduct. The original article will remain available online to preserve the scholarly record and will be clearly marked as retracted. Author response: The authors acknowledged the concerns and requested an opportunity to correct the article. After further editorial assessment, the Editorial Office maintained the decision to retract the article.
